A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A-H. Corresponding theoretical and experimental content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original training experiments on the synthetic trigger-conditional task, including attention statistics and multilayer model results in Section 4, Appendix C, and Figures 3-8.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and their results, including the softmax/ReLU comparisons and attention patterns across layers and heads.

M1.justification: The softmax and position-scaled ReLU architectures in Section 3.4, their input-output mapping, and the explicit ReLU construction in Appendix F are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic trigger-conditional averaging task with uniformly sampled content coordinates. The added GPT-2 discussion concerns cited research, not a new evaluation by this work.

E2.justification: The same softmax and ReLU models participate in the single-layer and multilayer comparisons. The added citations introduce no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sequence length 16, input dimension 16, model configurations, training settings, and the 1000-example evaluation with trigger position 8 are retained. Section 3.2.3 calls the existing loss a worst-case loss without changing its formula.

E4.justification: The comparisons examining normalization and the analyses of sink occurrence across layers and heads are unchanged. Appendix C and Figures 6-8 retain the same supplementary evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean and standard deviation of attention weights across 1000 test examples in Figure 3. Neither adds seed information, repeated-training statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 3-8 contain identical result images, and the reported experimental outcomes are retained. Changing 'pre-trigger' or 'before the trigger' to 'non-trigger' clarifies patterns already shown in the figures and described elsewhere in v1.

T1.justification: The theorem statements, assumptions, constructions, and proofs are unchanged; Appendices D-G match apart from pagination and whitespace. The revised loss description retains the same mathematical definition.

C1.justification: Both versions claim sink necessity for the analyzed softmax models and a sink-free ReLU solution. The abstract's added optimization-versus-necessity framing and 'in some settings' qualification make explicit the scope already stated in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds the interpretation that functional necessity may lead optimization to realize sinks through different architecture-specific circuits, connecting the theory to cited GPT-2 findings. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same optimizer, learning rates, batch size, stopping criterion, and data-generation details. The experiment-reproduction code link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Alberti et al. (2023) and Kidger and Lyons (2020) to contextualize the loss formulation, plus Ran-Milo et al. (2026b) and a short GPT-2 circuit discussion in Appendix H. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to the abstract, loss explanation, experimental descriptions, related-work paragraph, and acknowledgments. Section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3's caption explicitly identifies Theorems 1 and 3 and replaces 'before the trigger' with 'at non-trigger positions.' Text reflows across columns and pages, while all eight figure images and their numbering remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 improves clarity and internal consistency by aligning the positional descriptions in Figure 3 and Section 4 with the existing evidence. The loss explanation and added related-work connection provide useful context. These are limited gains: the theoretical support, experiments, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
